1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the account via owner(req) from the server-side session's s.user (accounts.get(s.user)), never from a client-supplied identifier, so only the session owner can access their MFA settings.

2.why: Verification challenges are scoped per session (r.s.identityCode) and TOTP/recovery secrets per account, so a code issued to one session/account cannot be used by another.

3.why: /api/authenticator/confirm only sets r.a.mfa = true and never invalidates the current or any other existing sessions, so sessions established before MFA enablement continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt() before storing in r.a.otp) and recovery codes are stored as SHA-256 peppered hashes, never in plaintext.

5.why: All secrets, OTPs, session IDs and recovery codes are generated via crypto.getRandomValues through bytes()/secureHex()/randomFrom() with rejection sampling, a CSPRNG source.

6.why: The only cookie (mfa_session) is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps CSRF token, secret and codes only in in-memory JS variables—no localStorage/sessionStorage or readable cookies are used.

7.why: Server-side validation is applied: email regex plus length caps at login, six() regex for OTP entries, rec() regex for recovery codes, and JSON body shape checking in body().

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent/createElement (msg, log, codes, setup key), innerHTML is used only with static templates, and a nonce-based CSP blocks inline script injection.

9.why: The application contains no redirect functionality or redirect parameters at all, so no open redirect is possible, though no explicit allow-list mechanism exists either.

10.why: headers() sets CSP (with per-request nonce), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict', carrying all three required attributes.

12.why: While server error output is generic and nothing is server-logged, the client deliberately writes the identity OTP, provisioning secret/URI, and all backup codes into the browser console and an on-page 'Logs' panel ('TESTING ONLY — ...' log calls).

13.why: Identity codes carry a used flag and 10-minute expiry, TOTP counters are recorded in acceptedTotpCounters to reject reuse within a ±1 window of 30-second steps, and recovery codes are deleted on use with a one-year expiry.

14.why: Login, identity, authenticator and recovery verification each track failure counters and impose a 5-minute lockout after MAX_FAILURES (5) attempts, returning 429.

15.why: Login deletes the old session and issues a fresh ID (sessions.delete(old.id); newSession()), current() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
